text_before: We propose a weakly supervised semantic segmentation method that utilizes large quantities and diversities in unlabeled videos to produce accurate, high-resolution results quickly. Our method utilizes motion cues found in video sequences to localize objects and classes. These cues are learned by an offline classifier, and their predictions are used as initial seed sets to propagate via graph cut optimization. Our method utilizes both spatial and temporal structural information, giving our system a good performance over static image-only learning frameworks as reported in literature. We also incorporate recent work, such as Deep Features (a Convolutional Neural Network), to improve overall accuracy and efficiency without significantly increasing run time cost. Our method significantly outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods such as PropNet and LTFS2K+N on public benchmark datasets such as Cityscapes, MPII, and CamVid, which are densely and significantly varied in their labeled regions.

"Ingredients:

1/2 cup butter

1/2 cup white sugar

1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder

1/2 cup all-purpose flour

1/2 cup chopped walnuts

1/2 cup semisweet chocolate chips

1/2 cup white chocolate chips

1/2 cup sweetened condensed milk

1/2 cup instant coffee granules

1/2 cup confectioners' sugar

Directions:

Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x9 inch pan.

In a medium bowl, cream together the butter, sugar and cocoa powder. Mix in the flour and walnuts. Press into the bottom of the prepared pan.

Bake for 15 minutes in the preheated oven. Remove from oven and sprinkle with chocolate chips. Return to oven for 1 minute, or until chocolate chips are soft. Spread chocolate chips evenly over the crust.

In a small saucepan, combine the white chocolate chips, condensed milk and instant coffee. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until smooth. Pour over the chocolate chips. Refrigerate until firm.

Remove from refrigerator and sprinkle with confectioners' sugar. Cut into bars."

Recipe posted by "Mommy2003" on Jan. 1, 2003.

He said a compulsory vaccination program would introduce "a disease status that provides clarity and confidence to farmers, Government, and the wider public."
